title: 11. skill description budget -- one globbed assertion for the whole plugin

labels.name: skill
labels.description: Adds or changes a plugin skill

body:
## Context

Skill auto-invocation is description-match driven, and descriptions compete for a shared listing budget of roughly one percent of the context window. On overflow, Claude Code drops descriptions starting from the least-recently-invoked skill. The pre-planning suite adds eight near-identically phrased `SKILL.md` files on top of the four that exist -- precisely the shape that degrades -- and the beats a user runs least lose their descriptions first.

The arithmetic, because it is what turns a documented risk into a deliverable. An earlier measurement put the four existing descriptions at 349, 390, 519 and 647 characters -- 1,905 total, comfortable -- but that record is gone, so re-measure before relying on it. Twelve at that mean is roughly 5,700. One percent of a 200,000-token window is about 2,000 tokens, call it 8,000 characters, and that is shared with every other installed plugin, every project skill and every personal skill the user has. This plugin alone would claim most of it. Nothing in the chain is a hard error; the failure is silent, asymmetric, and lands on the beats used least.

The enforcement problem is separate, and it is why this is an issue rather than a line in another one. `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_skill_contract.py` checks frontmatter against three hard-coded constants and does not cover `skills/tdd-review/SKILL.md` at all; that skill's own description pin ended up in `skills/tdd-review/tests/test_test_principles_contract.py`, a different directory under a different test's name. **A per-skill constant list did not survive four skills and will not survive twelve.** Enumerate by glob, once, for the whole plugin.

Originally folded into issue 09 (#23). Separated because it is plugin-wide, constrains files eight other issues own, needs its own doc re-verification, and has nothing to do with reporting where a slug is in the chain.

## Blocked by

Nothing mechanically -- the test can land against the four existing skills and strengthen as siblings arrive. Sequence it early anyway: the trigger-phrase rule is the epic's constraint 4, cheap from the first beat and expensive to retrofit across eight.

## Deliverables

- **A globbed test**, in a location no single skill owns:
  - `skills/*/SKILL.md` -- every skill, not only the new ones -- for the **aggregate ceiling**. A budget is shared by definition, so measuring only the eight new descriptions measures nothing. The ceiling is a literal number with its derivation in a comment beside it: window size, the one-percent figure, characters per token, the share this plugin may claim. A ceiling with no recorded arithmetic is a number the next contributor raises rather than a constraint.
  - `skills/product-*/SKILL.md` for the per-skill rules: under the per-skill cap, and a distinguishing trigger phrase in the **first sentence**. The `product-` prefix is part of that surface but a prefix alone does not distinguish `product-spec` from `product-requirements`; the first sentence must name the artifact or question the skill owns before it says anything the siblings also say.
- **A written `disable-model-invocation` evaluation** covering all twelve skills, carried into the epic. Starting position, to be confirmed or overturned below: `product-status`, `product-brief` and `product-review` stay model-invocable, because those are the cold-start surfaces -- a user says "where am I", "write me a product brief", or "review this brief" without knowing the suite exists. The five mid-and-late-chain beats are the candidates, because each is reached from a chain position `product-status` reports rather than cold. The mechanism is not novel: `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md` already ships it.

## Constraints

- **Re-verify one load-bearing fact first**: does `disable-model-invocation: true` remove a description from the model-facing listing entirely, or only stop auto-invocation while the description still occupies budget? If the latter, the mitigation frees nothing, the evaluation is worthless, and the only lever left is shorter descriptions -- which changes the recommendation but not the aggregate assertion. Land the answer in the PR; do not ship on the assumption.
- **Reconcile the per-skill cap to one number in one place.** Two figures are in circulation: 1,536 characters for `description` plus `when_to_use`, and the under-1024 that `test_test_principles_contract.py` asserts. Only the second is in the repository and neither has a live citation, so re-verify against the docs. Pick one and leave exactly one assertion of it -- if the 1024 survives it moves, if the globbed one supersedes it the old one is deleted, not left beside it.
- **Both assertions fail loudly with the measured number**, since a budget test whose failure does not say by how much is one the next contributor guesses at.
- **`test_skill_contract.py` still passes unchanged.** This adds coverage; it does not take over that file's existing assertions.
- **This issue may edit a sibling's `description` frontmatter and nothing else** if one landed non-compliant first. The alternative is a test that is red on arrival for a reason its own deliverables cannot fix.
- Inherits the epic's constraints.

## Out of scope

Every skill's behaviour, body, references and tests -- this touches `description` lines and adds one test file. Adding `disable-model-invocation: true` to any beat: this issue writes the evaluation, each beat's issue makes the change. Rewriting the four existing descriptions, unless the aggregate cannot pass without it, in which case say so in the PR rather than editing quietly. The artifact family, the substrate, any template.

## References

- The baseline figures above (349 / 390 / 519 / 647) come from a prior measurement whose record was not committed. Re-measure the four shipped `SKILL.md` descriptions as the first step, and derive the ceiling from what you actually find rather than from those numbers.
- The budget, the per-skill cap, `disable-model-invocation`, the drop rule: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- The contract this extends and the enumerate-by-constant pattern it replaces: `skills/deep-plan/tests/test_skill_contract.py`.
- The assertion to reconcile: `skills/tdd-review/tests/test_test_principles_contract.py`.
- In-repo precedent for `disable-model-invocation: true`: `skills/deep-plan/SKILL.md`.
- Where this came from: issue 09 (#23), which originally carried it.
